title: Attribute billing for function/tool outputs invoked during generation
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Problem: When the runtime surfaces model 'function_call' objects (tool invocations) that trigger additional I/O or model calls (e.g., external search, DB lookups, or nested inference), token accounting is currently attributing all emitted data to the original user request indiscriminately. This causes two classes of errors: (1) under/over-charging customers when tool outputs are generated by third-party services or by separate downstream model calls, and (2) duplicated billing when tool output is streamed as sideband messages and then materialized into the main response.

Goal: Produce a robust, auditable attribution model so every token/byte in the final delivered experience is labeled with an origin (user-input, model-generated, tool-output, downstream-model-call). Ensure per-customer invoices and quota enforcement reflect only the portions they should be billed for, while preserving correct capacity accounting for reserved/dedicated pools.

Scope: Server-side behavior for hosted API and Dedicated runtime paths (streaming and non-streaming). Excludes on-prem install variable configuration beyond hooks documented in this ticket.

Non-goals: Changing pricing model. Modifying client SDK usage surfaces. Native pricing policy changes will be handled separately once attribution is reliable.
acceptance_criteria: Every token/stream fragment has provenance metadata emitted to the metering pipeline (origin: user|model|tool|downstream-model|external).
Invoice and quota calculations use provenance to include/exclude tokens per billing rules (e.g., tool outputs labeled external are not customer-billed unless configured).
No increase in duplicate counts observed in test harness for streaming function_call scenarios (<= 0.1% regression allowed against baseline).
End-to-end tests covering nested function calls (model->tool->model) produce deterministic attribution and ledger entries.
Observability: dashboard shows breakdown by origin per-route and per-customer; alerts on attribution anomalies (sudden >5% tool-token spike).
implementation_notes: Add lightweight provenance header on internal transport messages carrying tokenized chunks: provenance=(origin, request_id, call_depth). Keep headers compact to avoid extra tokenization cost.
Metering pipeline: extend events with origin tag and event_type (token_debit|token_credit|compute_ms). Keep schema flat to avoid downstream parsing changes.

Streaming: sideband frames that carry tool outputs must be normalized into the primary stream with unified offsets before final tokenization pass to avoid double-counting. Implement idempotency marker for sideband->main handoff.

Downstream-model calls: attribute tokens to the top-level request unless operator flag 'pass-through-billing' is set; for external services, default to 'external' origin. Provide per-tenant toggle in Console later.
Reserved capacity: ensure compute accounting still charges capacity consumption to the tenant consuming GPU cycles, even if tokens are marked external. Separate billing vs capacity accounting paths.
Backward compat: default origin for any event without provenance is 'model' to be conservative; we will backfill known flows in rollout window.
Provide an ingestion adapter that maps existing ledger events to new origin-tagged records for continuity in historical reports.
Add unit + integration tests in the metering harness that replay recorded function_call sessions (use synthetic traffic from tools/testdata/func_calls/) and verify ledger outputs.
testing_plan: Create deterministic replay fixture: function_call nested chain 3 levels deep with mocked tool outputs. Verify ledger entries and summed token counts match expected breakdown.
Fuzz streaming path: interleave partial tool sideband frames, reconnects, and resume semantics; verify idempotent final ledger rows.
Simulate reserved capacity tenant and hosted tenant differences; assert capacity_ms charged to correct tenant even when tokens are marked external.
Run long-tail production shadow run for 72 hours for 5% sample of incoming function_call traffic and compare new vs legacy billing deltas.
Security review: ensure provenance headers cannot be spoofed by external clients (validate in proxy layer).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests (roll forward ability).
2) Canary: enable provenance tags + metering consumer in staging; run synthetic replays.
3) Shadow: 5% prod traffic routing to new metering consumer (no invoice changes). Monitor anomaly metrics for 48-72h.
4) Opt-in: enable per-tenant console toggle for customers to opt into 'bill-tool-outputs' for 2 weeks.
5) Global: flip to default new attribution and publish release notes explaining behavior change and how to interpret invoices.
Rollback: revert metering consumer and toggle to previous mapping; keep shadow data for investigation.
Timeline: target production enablement by runtime-1.22 (2026-04), with canary in 2026-03-20.
monitoring_metrics: provenance_missing_rate (percent of events lacking provenance header)
tool_output_double_count_rate (cases where same fragment counted twice)
capacity_charged_mismatch_rate (cases where token attribution excludes tenant but capacity_ms charged elsewhere)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Clients may rely on current implicit billing; mitigation: 2-week opt-in and clear release notes + examples.
Risk: Provenance tags increase event size and processing cost; mitigation: compact header encoding and aggressive sampling for low-throughput tenants.
Risk: Spoofed sideband frames could manipulate attribution; mitigation: validate provenance at proxy and sign internal messages where feasible.
Risk: Edge-case nested calls causing cycles; mitigation: enforce max_call_depth=5 and detect loops emitting 'external' fallback.
